program: Wingless raw-input to representation to reasoning to generation chain
question: Does changing only value-anchor selection from occurrence-margin-first to precision-first eliminate the R3 cross-class anchor collision and restore operand/template invariance while leaving operation inference, reasoning, and generation unchanged?
hypothesis: On the byte-identical R3 corpus and split, the unchanged R3 operation anchors/model plus precision-first value-anchor selection will choose eight distinct value anchors with zero equality to any operation anchor, reach at least 0.98 training and 0.95 held-out left/right accuracy with zero decode failures, preserve at least 0.95 held-out operation accuracy, and restore at least 0.90 held-out reasoning and exact raw-output accuracy.

portfolio_context.note: R3 itself produced a direct falsification of occurrence-margin-first anchor selection via a sealed cross-class anchor collision

prior_evidence.diagnosis: value class one selected the same ambiguous raw anchor as operation or because occurrence margin outranked class precision after equal positive coverage

repair_boundary.unchanged: R3 raw candidate windows, example-level supervision, operation-anchor selection, operation histogram inference, byte-order operand role assignment, corpus, split, target rules, reasoning learner, generator, lookup control, scientific chain thresholds

value_anchor_selection.candidate_windows: unchanged raw width 2..7 candidates from training instructions
value_anchor_selection.selection_order: highest positive-example coverage; then highest positive precision; then largest positive-minus-negative mean occurrence margin; then widest byte span; then lexicographically smallest raw bytes
value_anchor_selection.operation_selection: unchanged R3 order: coverage, occurrence margin, precision, width, lexicographic
value_anchor_selection.post_selection_constraints: none; cross-class anchor equality is measured, not prohibited by the selector

validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.
R4 calls the byte-identical R1 corpus constructor and retains all R3 downstream mechanisms.
Operation anchors and operation-count inference use the unchanged R3 selector/model.
Only the value-anchor candidate comparison order changes, exactly as preregistered.
Candidate induction receives training labels only at example level and no evaluator byte spans, word boundaries, parser, or tokenizer.
Value anchor duplicate/collision metrics are post-selection diagnostics and do not alter selection.
Operand roles remain assigned only from raw anchor occurrence byte order.
Reasoning consumes predicted R4 representations and generation remains teacher-free.
Full Go regression passes before the probe and all metrics are finite.
No external model, network call, capacity growth, threshold adaptation, or post-result tuning occurs.

classification_rules.supported: All validity criteria and all frozen thresholds pass.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes and R4 materially improves operands/end-to-end output over R3 but at least one frozen threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but precision-first value anchors do not materially improve the chain over R3.
classification_rules.incomplete: Compute interruption prevents the frozen matrix.
classification_rules.invalid: Any corpus/split drift, operation-model drift, semantic-span leakage, parser/tokenizer use, downstream mechanism drift, capacity, or qualification criterion fails.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: No corpus, candidate set, operation selector, value selector order, operand rule, downstream learner, generator, control, metric, threshold, or interpretation may change after primary output.
